newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds pare gains taking cues from U.S. markets.
newsitem.headline: Bunds pare gains taking cues from U.S. markets.

text.p: German Bunds, still taking cues from the U.S. market, posted gains near the end of Tuesday's session but were off the day's highs, receding after the U.S. market retreated after key economic data.
Bunds traded up 15 basis points at 97.30 shortly before the close of trading, nearer to the day's low at 97.08 than the high of 97.44.

While prices moved higher during the most of the session, dealers said the market lacked sufficient momentum to break through new resistance levels. Now the test was to see if Bunds could close above the key 97.33 level, dealers said.
Dealers were slightly sceptical about the market's upward potential, saying that the economic recovery may again lose speed, sending interest rates higher at the long end of the yield curve.
Today attention again centred on U.S. markets which opened higher as investors returned to the market after giving it a pummelling late last week after a spate of economic data.

But strong U.S. consumer confidence numbers rising to a six-year high of 109.4 in August from a revised reading of 107.0 in July, forced Treasuries to retreat while retaining overall gains. "The same happened here," a dealer said.
Dealers said the German market may be suffering from having run out of steam, particulary after the Bundesbank wiped out most interest rate speculation after slashing its repo rate last Thursday.
The central bank surprised markets by cutting its repo rate by 30 basis points moving it to three percent, the first reduction since February.
Subsequently dealers see the market struggling in a range in the next few days, trying to move higher but possibly losing even more steam to fall lower.
